name: relative_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Within a sector (e.g., private banks), the intraday return spread between the strongest and weakest stock tends to revert after reaching an extreme. If HDFC Bank is +1.5% and ICICI Bank is -0.5% at 11:00 AM (a 2% spread), the spread tends to narrow by EOD because both stocks share the same fundamental drivers (interest rates, NPA concerns). The excess spread is caused by timing differences in institutional order flow — one stock gets bought first, the other follows. The inefficiency exists because most intraday traders focus on absolute returns, not relative performance within a sector. The edge persists because monitoring relative spreads across multiple sectors in real-time requires infrastructure beyond typical retail setups.
universe: NIFTY 200 constituents, grouped by GICS sector
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND same sector has >=3 stocks meeting liquidity criteria

long.confirmation: relative_zscore[t] > relative_zscore[t-1] (relative underperformance starting to narrow)

short.confirmation: relative_zscore[t] < relative_zscore[t-1] (relative outperformance starting to narrow)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close; optionally pair with opposite position in sector ETF/strongest stock

exit.stop_loss: relative_zscore reaches ±3.0 (divergence deepening) OR 0.5% loss on the leg
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.2% once relative_zscore within ±0.5 of zero
exit.signal_exit: exit if sector itself starts moving against the position (macro shift)

risk.position_sizing: 1L per leg; if paired, 1L long + 1L short

filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (need relative data to stabilize) or after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: both stocks in the pair must have adequate volume
filters.trend_filter: prefer trades when the sector is range-bound (|sector_median_return| < 1%)
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has a stock-specific event (earnings, corporate action) causing the relative divergence
other_filters: minimum 3 stocks in the sector passing liquidity filter for meaningful median

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — relative sector reversion requires real-time multi-stock infrastructure, barrier to entry

weaknesses: If relative divergence is caused by stock-specific news (upgrade/downgrade), it may not revert — event filter is imperfect
Running on single-stock basis (not paired) exposes to market beta; paired trading doubles costs and complexity
Sectors with few liquid stocks (e.g., only 3-4 names) have unreliable median estimates
prior_art: Pairs trading and relative value is foundational stat arb (Gatev et al., 2006). Sector relative strength is documented in Faber (2007). Intraday sector-relative reversion is less studied — most pairs trading literature is daily horizon. ETF stat arb (Avellaneda & Lee, 2010) is related but uses ETF baskets rather than sector medians.
notes: Edge math (single-leg): 0.55 * 50bps - 0.45 * 36bps = 27.5 - 16.2 = 11.3 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 0.3 bps. If paired: double costs to ~22 bps, but spread has lower volatility so stops are tighter, improving W:L. Need backtest to compare paired vs single-leg.
